info.title: diff-reviewer platform API
info.description:
The review platform: the repositories whose pull requests it reviews, and one review job per review. A job moves `pending → queued → running → draft → approved → posted`; `rejected` is a discarded draft, `stale` a draft whose pull request has moved on, and `failed` a run that ended without a review.

Three credentials, none standing in for another. The password (`$DIFF_REVIEWER_PASSWORD`) is accepted only by `POST /api/login`, which sets the session cookie; failed password logins are rate-limited (an immediate `429` with `Retry-After`), and the API token signs in there too, unlimited. Every route under `/api/v1/` needs the session cookie or the API token (`$DIFF_REVIEWER_API_TOKEN_FILE`) as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Every route under `/api/agent/v1/` needs the agent token (`$DIFF_REVIEWER_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE`) as a bearer, and nothing else reaches it; an agent's requests go through kleis, which supplies it.

Every write must be `application/json` (`415` otherwise). Every write to a job under `/api/v1/` names the job's `version` as last read, and is a `409` if the job has changed since. A request the server fails on is a `500` whose reason goes to the server log; a method a route does not answer is a `405`. Collections answer `{"items": [...]}`. Instants are RFC 3339 in UTC; an absent value is `null`.

Each repository has a rubric document — a default rubric and the pull request types its reviews tell apart, each with a rubric and the categories its comments are filed under — written whole and versioned (`/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{name}/rubrics`). Every write of a job's review, by the agent, a person or (once posted) GitHub, is kept as a revision (`/api/v1/jobs/{id}/revisions`).

post.summary: Exchange the password, or the API token, for a session cookie

200.description: Signed in; sets the session cookie.

post.description:
Password attempts are counted per client address — an IPv6 client per /64 — the socket's peer, or, for a request from the proxy `--trusted-proxy` names, the last address of its `X-Forwarded-For`. After 5 failures from one address within 15 minutes every password attempt from it, right or wrong, is a `429` for a delay that starts at 15 seconds and doubles with each further failure (at most 15 minutes). After 100 failures from all addresses together, every password attempt is a `429` for a while. A refusal is immediate; `Retry-After` says how long. A success clears its address's count.

The API token signs in too, and no limit counts it or refuses it: it is how the operator gets in while password attempts from everywhere are refused.

get.summary: Whether the caller is signed in

200.description: Every repository, by owner and name.

mode.description: `staged` (default): a person approves each review before it is posted. `direct`: posted as soon as the agent submits it.

autoReview.description: Default `false`: only the jobs asked for are reviewed.

put.description: Names are stored in lower case, as GitHub compares them. The body replaces the repository's settings: a field it omits takes its default.

delete.description: Its jobs are kept: they are the record of reviews that happened.

post.summary: Ask for a review of a pull request

headSha.description: The head commit the review is for: a whole commit id (40 or 64 hex digits; an abbreviation is a `400`), stored in lower case. Queueing checks it is still the pull request's head, and makes the job `stale` if it is not.

put.description: The body is `{"version": n, "review": {...}}`. Allowed while the job is `pending`, `draft`, `approved` or `rejected` (`409` otherwise: the agent may still be writing it, or it is history), and makes it a `draft`: an approval was of the review as it was. Each comment must name a file and lines `1 ≤ start_line ≤ end_line`, and say something. `409` while a post of the job may have reached GitHub (`postStartedAt` is set). Each comment's `category` is checked against the rubric version the job was reviewed against (the current one if none). Comments without an `id` are given one, and the review is appended to the job's revisions as a person's.

post.summary: Make a person's decision on a job
post.description: A person's moves only: `draft → approved | rejected | stale`, `approved → draft`, `rejected → draft`, and `failed → pending` to run the review again (which clears `queueEntry` and `error`; the next attempt is queued under a new orchestra `external_id`). Queueing, running, the agent's draft and posting are the platform's own, and no request makes them — posting is asked for with `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/post`. Any other move is a `409`, and so is approving a job without a readable review. `409` while a post of the job may have reached GitHub (`postStartedAt` is set).

post.summary: Post an approved review to GitHub
post.description: Posts the job's review to its pull request — submitted, pinned to `headSha` with every comment on the right-hand side, its body ending in the marker `<!-- diff-reviewer job <id> -->` — and then marks the job `posted`, recording GitHub's id, URL and body of the review in `postedReview`. The event is the review's decision, except on a pull request the operator (`DIFF_REVIEWER_GITHUB_LOGIN`) wrote, where an approval or a request for changes is posted as a comment and `postNote` says so. The job must be `approved` and at the `version` named, its review valid and its comments on the diff (`409` otherwise). Posting is claimed (`postStartedAt`) immediately before the request to GitHub; a claim less than three times that request's timeout old is a `409`, as a post that may still be under way. An older claim is settled first: the pull request's reviews by the operator are searched for the marker, and a review found is recorded rather than posted again. A `4xx` from GitHub clears the claim and leaves the job `approved` with the reason in `error` (a `502` that carries the job). No answer or a `5xx` keeps the claim, even when the review is not found yet, so the next attempt looks again before posting. `503` when the platform has no GitHub token.

502.description: GitHub refused the review or could not be reached.

get.description: The unified diff of the pull request at the job's head commit, from its merge base with the base commit — what GitHub shows as the pull request's diff. Fetched from GitHub once per base and head and then kept. `409` for a job that names no head commit yet; `502` when GitHub cannot be read; `503` when the platform has no GitHub token. `413` for a diff past `--max-diff-bytes`.

parameters.name: X-Diff-Reviewer-Job
parameters.description: The job the agent's prompt named (`--job`). Without it, the request is about the pull request's only queued or running job, and with two it is a `409`: an older run must not take over a newer review.

get.summary: The review the agent is running
get.description: The job the agent runs (see `X-Diff-Reviewer-Job`), `queued` or `running`; reading a `queued` one moves it to `running`. `404` when no review of the pull request is being run. `409` too when the repository's rubric cannot be read by this build.

200.description: The job, as the agent needs it.

parameters.name: X-Diff-Reviewer-Job
parameters.description: The job the agent's prompt named (`--job`). Without it, the request is about the pull request's only queued or running job, and with two it is a `409`: an older run must not take over a newer review.

get.description: The running job's diff, as `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/diff` gives it, as plain text.

parameters.name: X-Diff-Reviewer-Job
parameters.description: The job the agent's prompt named (`--job`). Without it, the request is about the pull request's only queued or running job, and with two it is a `409`: an older run must not take over a newer review.

post.description: The job must be `running` and `headSha` must be its head (`409` otherwise). The review must be one GitHub would take (`400`, saying what to fix): at most 200 inline comments, a summary unless it approves, and every comment's lines in one hunk of the diff's new side. `prType` must be one of the rubric's pull request types, or null when it names none, and each comment's `category` one of that type's categories (see `InlineComment`) (`400`). Comments without an `id` are given one. The job becomes a `draft`, recording `prType` and the rubric's version, and the review is the first of its revisions. For a repository in `direct` mode the platform then posts it — always as a comment, whatever its decision, which the job keeps; if posting fails the job is left `approved` with the reason in `error`, and the submission still stands; when the post's outcome was unknown and it is found not to have reached GitHub, the workers post it again, up to 3 posts in all.

prType.description: The name of the pull request type reviewed, one of `prTypes`; null when there are none.

status.description: `draft`, or `posted` (or `approved`, if posting failed) in `direct` mode.

post.summary: Settle a post whose outcome is unknown, without posting
post.description: For a job whose `postStartedAt` is set — a post that may have reached GitHub. The pull request's reviews by the operator are searched for the job's marker. Found, the job is `posted`, with GitHub's record in `postedReview`. Not found and the claim older than its window (three times the post's timeout), the claim is cleared and the job left `approved`, free to be moved back to `draft`, rejected, posted again or made `stale`. Not found within the window, a `409`: the post may still be under way. Reviews that cannot be read leave the claim as it is: a `502` that carries the job. `409` too for a job that is not `approved`, not at `version`, or has no claim. The workers do the same on every pass for every claim past its window, so a claim is settled without this too. In a `direct` repository the workers then post a review that did not reach GitHub again, as a comment, up to 3 posts of the job in all; past that it is left `approved` with the reason in `error`.

200.description: The job: `posted`, or `approved` without its claim.

502.description: GitHub's reviews could not be read; the claim stands.

get.summary: The history of a job's review
get.description: Every write of the job's review, oldest first: the agent's submission, each person's edit, and what GitHub holds once it is posted. What the agent drafted beside what was posted.
The current version; version 0 with an empty document when there is none yet. `404` for a repository that is not registered.

put.description: The body is the whole document with the version it replaces, as last read (`409` if that is no longer the current one). It becomes the next version, and the one it replaces stays in the history. A type's `description`, `rubric` and `categories` default to empty. `400` for a type or category without a name or with the name of another, past 50 types or 50 categories a type, or a rubric past 65536 bytes. The answer of a `GET` may be sent back as it is, edited: its `owner`, `name`, `createdAt` and `documentError` are not kept as the document's, and fields this build does not know, on the document, a type or a category, are kept.

version.description: The version last read; 0 when the repository had none.

get.summary: Every version of a repository's rubric document
get.description: Newest first. A job's `rubricVersion` names one of them.

bearerAuth.description: The API token ($DIFF_REVIEWER_API_TOKEN_FILE). The password is not accepted here.

agentBearer.description: The agent token ($DIFF_REVIEWER_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE), which kleis injects into an agent's requests. Reaches `/api/agent/v1/` only.

Error.description: The request was refused; `error` says why.

autoReview.description: Whether the platform lists the repository's open pull requests itself and makes a job for each new head commit (GitHub draft pull requests excepted).

status.description: A `JobStatus`; a status a newer build wrote is shown as it is, and the job is read-only to this one.

queueEntry.description: The orchestra queue entry running the review, once queued: the latest, after following `continuedBy`.

reviewError.description: Why the stored review cannot be read by this build, when it cannot; `review` is then null and the job is read-only.

version.description: Incremented by every write; sent back with the next one.

baseSha.description: The pull request's base commit, from GitHub, once known.

title.description: The pull request's title, from GitHub, once known.

prBody.description: The pull request's description, from GitHub, once known.

error.description: What the platform's last step on the job failed with — queueing, the run, posting — until one succeeds.

prType.description: The pull request type the agent said it reviewed: one of the rubric's types, at `rubricVersion`.

attempts.description: How many times the job has been queued on orchestra.

postStartedAt.description: When posting last began, while its outcome is not known: the claim that keeps the review from being posted twice. While it is set the job cannot leave `approved`, have its review edited or be made `stale` (`409`); posting it again, or `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/reconcile`, settles it.

postNote.description: How the review was posted when that differs from its decision: in `direct` mode, or on a pull request the operator wrote, an approval or request for changes is posted as a comment.

postedReview.description: The review as GitHub holds it, once posted: what was posted, which after a post whose outcome was unknown is GitHub's record rather than the job's own review.

rubricVersion.description: The version of the repository's rubric document the review was checked against: recorded with the agent's submission; null for a job the agent has not reviewed.

postAttempts.description: How many times posting the review has been attempted (claimed, and GitHub asked). In a `direct` repository the platform posts on its own at most 3 times in all.

comments.description: At most 200. A comment's lines must lie in one hunk of the diff's new side.

Review.description: A `comment` or `request_changes` review must have a non-empty `body`; GitHub refuses either without one. Fields this build does not know, on the review or on a comment, are kept as they are.

suggestion.description: Replacement text for the lines, posted as a GitHub suggestion.

id.description: Stable within the review, and unique in it. A comment written without one is given one by the platform when the review is submitted or edited; one it has is kept. A review stored before ids existed gets them on its next write, not when it is read.

category.description: What the comment is about: when the repository's rubric names categories, one of those of the job's pull request type (or, if that type names none, of any type); otherwise free text.

severity.description: How much the comment matters. A severity this build does not know makes a stored review unreadable (`reviewError`), as an unknown decision does.

InlineComment.description: Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back on every round trip.

headSha.description: The commit to review, and the one a submission must name.

instructions.description: How to review and how to write the review, in markdown, followed by the repository's default rubric when it has one.

prTypes.description: The repository's pull request types, each with its rubric and categories: the agent picks the one that fits, reviews by its rubric and files its comments under its categories. Empty when the rubric names none.

examples.description: Past reviews to calibrate against; empty for now.

rubricVersion.description: The version of the rubric document these come from; null when the repository has none.

Category.description: Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back, a `PUT` of the document included.

name.description: Unique in the document; what a submission's `prType` names.

description.description: When the type applies: what the agent picks the type by.

rubric.description: How to review a pull request of this type, in markdown, on top of the default rubric. At most 65536 bytes.

categories.description: What a comment of a review of this type is filed under. Names are unique within the type.

PrType.description: Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back, a `PUT` of the document included.

RubricDocument.description: One version of a repository's rubric document. Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back, a `PUT` of the document included.

version.description: 1 for the first document and one more for each change; 0 for a repository that has none yet.

createdAt.description: When this version was written; null for version 0.

defaultRubric.description: How to review any pull request of the repository, in markdown; given to the agent in its `instructions`. At most 65536 bytes. Null only with `documentError`.

prTypes.description: The kinds of pull request the repository's reviews tell apart. Null only with `documentError`.

documentError.description: Why this build cannot read the stored document, when it cannot. The agent API then refuses the repository's reviews (`409`) rather than review without the rubric.

Revision.description: One write of a job's review.

version.description: The job's version the write made.

author.description: `agent` (the submission), `person` (an edit) or `github` (what GitHub holds once posted: the job's review with GitHub's body, without the marker, and the event it was posted as when known).

review.description: The review as written, as the JSON stored; not reinterpreted by this build.

reviewError.description: Why the stored review is not JSON, when it is not.
